sources.name: Plaid Transactions (/transactions/sync + webhooks)
sources.typicalLatency: Pending: hours after authorization (typical, unverified). Posted: typically 1-3 business days (unverified). Plaid 'typically checks… between one and four times per day, depending on the institution'. /transactions/refresh (a paid add-on) forces an on-demand check (<10 s typical, sometimes 30 s+). SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE signals new data. As of 2026-10-04.
sources.accessRequirements: Plaid contract and production approval. Transactions is billed per Item; Balance is pay-per-call. /transactions/refresh and Recurring Transactions are add-ons that need a product access request, and refresh has a separate per-request fee (list prices unverified). A backend must hold access tokens and receive webhooks.
sources.policyConstraints: Data Transparency Messaging consent scopes. consent_expiration_time and the 7-day PENDING_EXPIRATION webhook apply in EU/UK; the 7-day PENDING_DISCONNECT applies in US/CA. Users manage connections in Plaid Portal. The 1033 reauthorization field is 'not currently used' (Sept 2026 spec), so Plaid is not applying 1033-style 12-month expiry. The 1033 rule itself was enjoined in Oct 2025 and is under reconsideration (secondary).
dedupKeys: persistent_account_id (TAN institutions only: Chase, PNC, US Bank)
sources.rationale: The only turnkey ledger for the US and Canada (20 Link countries, none in IN/BR/AU/MX). Use it as the confirm-and-correct layer: pending within hours, posted in 1-3 business days, polled 1-4x/day, so it is POST-SPEND only. pending_transaction_id is populated only 'where applicable', `removed` must retract, running_balance is hidden from docs. MVP for US users (stream 11 said next; resolved to mvp because User B has no other ledger).

sources.name: Plaid Recurring Transactions (/transactions/recurring/get)
sources.typicalLatency: Daily-ish, following Transactions updates; RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE webhook.
sources.accessRequirements: Add-on to Transactions (product access request). At least 180 days of history recommended. Availability outside US/CA unverified.
sources.policyConstraints: Same as Plaid
sources.rationale: Paid add-on that predicts next dates (MATURE/EARLY_DETECTION/TOMBSTONED); best with >=180 days of history. Availability is US, CA and UK (Plaid docs seen via search on 2026-10-05; doc 01 said US/CA and doc 13 added EU - both corrected). A hint for BRAKE's own on-device recurring engine, not its replacement.

sources.name: India Account Aggregator (ReBIT/Sahamati FIP -> AA -> FIU)
sources.typicalLatency: On-demand fetch, bounded by consent Frequency (default purpose-102 rule: <= 1/day or <= 45 per calendar month). Posted transactions only. As of 2026-10-04.
sources.accessRequirements: BRAKE must be, or partner with, an FIU, defined in the RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction as 'an entity registered with and regulated by any financial sector regulator' (verified via a mirror of the MD text updated 22 Feb 2024). Integration goes through an AA or TSP (e.g. Finvu, Setu). Sahamati fair-use templates must be followed and the exact purpose text displayed.
sources.policyConstraints: Consent is created only in the AA's app. Default purpose-102 rule: PERIODIC, consent <= 1 year, FI data range <= 13 months, Data Life 31 days. CT019 (7 days) is an FIU-specific exception. Violations return HTTP 412. DPDP Rules 2025 were notified 13 Nov 2025, with most obligations from 13 May 2027.
dataFields: credit card (if obtainable): mcc, maskedCardNumber, dueDate, totalDueAmount, minDueAmount
creditcard: txnId, txnType, txnDate (date only), amount, valueDate, narration, statementDate, mcc, maskedCardNumber, currentDue, totalDueAmount, minDueAmount, dueDate
dedupKeys: UPI RRN parsed from narration (unverified format)
sources.rationale: Posted-only, high-quality deposit and card data with balance-after (currentBalance) and card MCC/due dates. BRAKE cannot be an FIU unless regulated, so it needs a regulated FIU partner. Purpose 102 fair-use: PERIODIC, consent <=1 year, <=13 months of data, <=1 fetch/day and <=45/month, Data Life 31 days (verified against Sahamati rules file 2026-10-05; doc 13's '24/day' was the generic API ceiling, not the purpose-102 rule). Streams disagreed (mvp/next/research): resolved to next because the partner is a precondition.

sources.name: UK Open Banking AIS (OBIE v4.0.1) incl. bank OB endpoints such as Revolut
sources.typicalLatency: Poll-based. Under UK-RTS Art. 36(5), <= 4 per 24 h without the user present and unlimited while the user is active (secondary; the FCA Handbook was unreachable). Same-day for Faster Payments.
sources.accessRequirements: Registered AISP under PSRs 2017, or agent/client of an authorised AISP (TrueLayer, Plaid UK, Tink, Yapily, etc.). The perimeter question needs counsel.
sources.policyConstraints: FCA PS21/19 replaced bank-side 90-day SCA with AISP 90-day consent reconfirmation. 2026 secondary sources still describe it as current, and the in-force date is unverified. Consumer Duty.
sources.rationale: Rich records (MerchantDetails incl. MCC, AuthorisationType, TransactionReference/FPID, purpose codes, PartyType Sole/Joint/Delegate, standing orders and direct debits). Poll-only: no transaction push events; <=4 unattended reads per 24 h, unlimited while the user is present; 90-day AISP reconfirmation. Needs AISP licence or agent route. No pending->booked link. Revolut OB carries no MCC.

sources.typicalLatency: Poll-based. Without the user present: <= 4 per 24 h unless a higher frequency is agreed bilaterally with the user's consent. Unlimited while the user is actively requesting (RTS Art. 36(5)).
sources.accessRequirements: AISP registration with a home NCA plus passporting, or agent/licence-as-a-service via Tink, Salt Edge, TrueLayer or Plaid (specifics unverified).
sources.policyConstraints: RTS 2018/389 Art. 36(5) access-frequency rule; Arts. 10/10a (as amended by Delegated Reg. 2022/2360, consolidated 2023-07-25) 180-day SCA renewal; GDPR.
sources.rationale: Post-spend ledger for EU users via a licensed aggregator; 4/day unattended cap, 180-day bank SCA renewal (Del. Reg. 2022/2360). Field population (endToEndId, mandateId, card MCC) varies per ASPSP, so key availability is an institution-level registry fact. PSD3/PSR not yet applicable as of 2026-10-04.

sources.name: Android NotificationListenerService (bank, card, UPI, wallet and messaging-app notifications)
sources.typicalLatency: Callback fires as soon as the notification is posted; seconds to minutes after payment depending on the issuer (unverified measurements)
sources.accessRequirements: User grants Notification access (Settings.ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS / ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS on API 30+). The service is declared with BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE. Not available on low-RAM devices running Android 10 or lower. Android 13+ restricted settings apply to sideloaded APKs. No NLS-specific Play declaration found (unverified for 2026).
sources.policyConstraints: Play User Data prominent-disclosure and consent rules, Data safety form, and spyware/stalkerware rules apply (details unverified). Android 15+ untrusted listeners receive redacted OTP-bearing notifications. A companion-device association or RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS is not obtainable or appropriate for BRAKE.
dedupKeys: SMS sender header + message timestamp (via messaging app)
sources.rationale: The Android MVP sensor: one user grant sees bank, card, UPI, wallet and (as rendered by Messages) SMS/RCS alerts within seconds, plus SCA/request-to-pay prompts and wallet tap notifications as template packs. No history API, OEM background killing, OTP redaction on Android 15+, restricted settings for sideloads, ePrivacy consent in the EU. One grant = many independent publishers, so fusion needs a channel key.

sources.accessRequirements: READ_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS are hard-restricted permissions that the installer on record must allow-list. sources.policyConstraints: Play SMS/Call Log policy treats exceptions as temporary and allows them only where no alternative exists (Play excerpt). A revision announced 2026-07-15 takes effect 2027-01-27 (unverified; secondary corroboration only). OTP SMS are withheld 3 h from non-exempt apps: Retriever-hash format before Android 17, WebOTP for all apps on Android 17, and standard OTP SMS for apps targeting API 37.
dedupKeys: exact body match with the NLS sighting of the same SMS
hash(normalized sender entity | normalized body) for broadcast vs provider duplicates
sources.rationale: Adds exact sender headers and months of history backfill at onboarding. Hard-restricted permission; Play allows it only for default handlers or an approved 'SMS-based money management' declaration (Play excerpt, secondary). Android 17 withholds OTP SMS for 3 h. Streams split mvp/next/research; resolved to next (opt-in upgrade after Play approval) with the listener as MVP capture.

Android 16 (API 36) auto-groups notifications on the app's behalf; if one app posts four or more notifications without a grouping, the system groups them. BRAKE should set explicit groups so user-requested reminders are not bundled with routine insights. The Android 16 and 17 'all apps' behavior-change pages list no other notification changes. Verified 2026-10-04.

Channels are required since Android 8.0; the app cannot change a channel's importance after creation, only the user can. BRAKE should use separate channels for questions, insights, digest and reminders. Verified 2026-10-04.

Android 15 (API 35) cooldown reduces the appearance, sound volume and vibration of repetitive notifications for up to two minutes.
